transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, or that I'm in the right place. 

I'm a supervisor for a sales team, and I really try to do a good job, but... I guess I've been making some kind of silly mistakes lately. Just on my sales reports, mostly. It's probably nothing major, but I'll do things like somehow copy the wrong numbers over from the team dashboard, or I'll miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check off. 

It's just a little embarrassing because I swear I thought I went over it carefully before turning it in. I really hate looking careless to my team or my bosses. I just want to make sure I'm doing things right... does that make sense as a reason to come in?
Do you notice this kind of difficulty concentrating or making careless mistakes happening in other parts of your life too—like at home or in personal tasks—or is it really just showing up at work?

Um... you know, I haven't really noticed it much outside of work. I try really hard to keep things running smoothly at home, so... I don't think I'm making mistakes like that with my personal stuff. Or, well, if I am, it's nothing major, just normal everyday things. 

I really try to be responsible, you know? So I'm pretty sure it's mostly just showing up at the office with those reports. Does that... is that a normal way for this to happen? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
When you're reviewing your reports, do you ever feel a strong urge to check them over and over because of a nagging thought that something might be wrong, even after you've already checked carefully?

No, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I definitely double-check my work because I want to do a good job, but... I don't get stuck doing it over and over or anything like that. I just try to be thorough. I don't have, like, nagging thoughts or anything weird like that. I just want to make sure the numbers are right so my boss is happy with it. Is that... that's just a normal thing to do, right? Checking your work?
Aside from work, do you find yourself worrying a lot about various things in your life—like your health, finances, or family—even when there's no clear reason to be concerned?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier like that. I mean, sure, everyone thinks about bills or making sure their family is okay, but... I don't sit around stressing over things for no reason. 

I try to stay pretty positive and just handle things as they come up. I definitely don't have, like, extreme anxiety or anything. I just want to do right by my family and my job, you know? That's a pretty normal way to feel, isn't it? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm overly anxious, because I'm really not.
Do you ever find that your focus on getting every detail exactly right causes you to fall behind on deadlines or have trouble finishing tasks on time?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean... I know how important deadlines are, especially being a supervisor. I really try my best to make sure things get turned in when they're supposed to. I definitely don't get so hung up on every little detail that I fall behind or anything like that. 

I just want the work to be good so my boss is happy, you know? But I know you have to actually finish the job, too. So I just do my best to balance doing it right with getting it done on time. That's... that's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I try really hard to be dependable like that. I hope that makes sense.
Thinking back to your school days or early adulthood, did you often make similar careless mistakes or have trouble staying focused on tasks back then, even before this job?

Well, um... I guess if I really think about it, yeah, it's kind of always been a thing for me. I mean, not in a bad way, just... I've always had a lot of energy, you know? 

My mom actually still brings up these old notes my teachers used to send home in elementary school. They'd say I, uh, rushed through my work a bit, or maybe misplaced my homework sometimes. And, well, I guess I had a habit of talking out of turn or needing a reminder to stay in my seat. But I was just a kid being a kid, right? Lots of kids have trouble sitting still or get a little too excited to share their thoughts. 

I definitely wasn't trying to be disruptive or anything. I just wanted to be involved. That's pretty normal for a young boy, isn't it? I mean, I eventually grew up and got a good job, so it couldn't have been too terrible, right?

Right now, outside of work, do you notice things like losing track of items, forgetting appointments, or feeling restless and distracted during everyday activities like reading, chores, or conversations?

Well, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, sometimes things slip my mind at home, too. But I think everyone gets a little forgetful when life gets busy, right? 

Like, occasionally I might forget to return a call—like I've been meaning to call my attorney back for a little bit now, but I just haven't gotten around to it. Or, you know, sometimes a bill might slip past me until I get a little reminder notice in the mail. And I guess there have been a couple of times I told the kids I'd pick something up for them and completely forgot until I walked through the door. 

But I always make it right, you know? I pay the bill as soon as I see the notice, and I always apologize to the kids and get them what I promised the next day. I'm really trying my best to stay on top of everything. It's just hard juggling it all sometimes, you know? That doesn't make me a bad dad or anything, right? I just have a lot on my plate.
Do you often find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble waiting your turn—like interrupting conversations or feeling like you need to be moving or doing something most of the time?

Well, um... I guess I do sometimes feel a little... antsy, maybe? But I think that's pretty normal when you're stuck sitting for a long time, right? 

Like, if I have to sit through a really long meeting at work, it almost feels like my body is... I don't know, kind of buzzing on the inside. I might shift around in my chair a bit, or maybe tap my foot just a little. Nothing crazy! And sometimes I might just make a quick excuse to get up and stretch my legs for a second, maybe grab some water. 

But I always come right back and pay attention. I try really hard not to be distracting to anyone else in the room. I mean, nobody likes sitting still for hours on end, do they? It's just a way to keep the blood flowing so I can stay focused. That's a good thing, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing my best at work.
Have your family members, friends, or coworkers ever told you that your forgetfulness, restlessness, or distractibility has caused real problems or frustration in your relationships with them?

Well, um... I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try hard to keep everyone happy, but I guess sometimes things slip through the cracks. 

My manager did, um, mention it recently. He actually put something about it in my formal review... just that I need to work on my follow-through and organization. But he knows I'm a hard worker! I always put in the effort, I just... get a little sidetracked sometimes. That's something I can fix, right? I'm definitely going to work on it.

And at home... well, my wife gets a little frustrated sometimes. She says she feels like she can't always count on me to finish things I start, or to remember things she asked me to do. It causes some arguments, which I hate. I never want her to feel like I don't care, because I really do! I just... I forget, or I get distracted by something else that needs doing. I'm trying to be better about writing things down so I don't let her down. That's a good strategy, isn't it? I really want to be a good husband and employee.
